Next.js generates separate client/server/edge webpack configs, injects React aliases and rules, then invokes the customer’s `config.webpack`; Module Federation subsequently resolves shared requests and webpack validates the resulting module graph/export bindings.

- [sg-evals/next.js--v13.5.6:packages/next/src/build/webpack-config.ts?L424-L470](/r/github.com/sg-evals/next.js--v13.5.6/-/blob/packages/next/src/build/webpack-config.ts?L424-L470) - `getBaseWebpackConfig`, the central Next.js webpack configuration generator.
- [sg-evals/next.js--v13.5.6:packages/next/src/build/webpack-config.ts?L152-L205](/r/github.com/sg-evals/next.js--v13.5.6/-/blob/packages/next/src/build/webpack-config.ts?L152-L205) - `createRSCAliases`; maps `react`, `react-dom`, `react-dom/client`, server variants, JSX runtimes, and React Server Components packages to Next’s compiled/vendored implementations.

- [sg-evals/webpack--v5.88.2:lib/dependencies/HarmonyExportImportedSpecifierDependency.js?L786-L860](/r/github.com/sg-evals/webpack--v5.88.2/-/blob/lib/dependencies/HarmonyExportImportedSpecifierDependency.js?L786-L860) - `_getErrors` compares terminal export bindings from multiple star-export sources and emits a `HarmonyLinkingError` when the same export resolves to different modules.

**Conflict mapping:** Next aliases exact requests such as `react-dom$` and `react-dom/client$` to compiled/vendored files. The customer’s Module Federation configuration then marks React/React-DOM as shared and may resolve a fallback or remote-provided module. Because aliases are applied before normal resolution, the shared request can resolve to Next’s aliased implementation while another Federation path resolves the package’s physical `react-dom/index.js`. Webpack then sees distinct module/export bindings in the same graph; its Harmony export-linking phase reports the conflicting `default`/module resolution or the missing `react-dom/client` path.

**Configuration implication:** preserve Next’s existing `config.resolve.alias`, `module.rules`, and `resolve` options; add Module Federation without replacing them. Share React and React-DOM as singletons with matching versions, and avoid overriding `react-dom`, `react-dom/client`, or Next’s layer-specific aliases. If Federation requires a fallback, explicitly point it at the same React/React-DOM implementation used by Next rather than allowing a second physical package copy.
